# Configuration settings

Every environment variable the backend reads, found by scanning the source rather than by
importing it — a variable read inside a function body is never reached by an import, so only
the source knows the whole set.

**255 settings.** 17 are *declared* in
`backend/config_registry.py`, which is the set `rackstatus.toml` can carry, the required-
setting preflight can demand, and `rackstatus.toml.example` lists. 120 are named in
`docs/ENVIRONMENT.md` — named, which is a weaker claim than explained: the check is
whether that document mentions the setting at all. It is not in this site yet; see
`docs/README.md` for why the migration is page-at-a-time.

## How a value is resolved

Highest wins (`core-designs.mdc` §5):

1. the active cluster's **high overlay** — identity, naming and connection from the catalog
2. **job env overrides** — `var/cache/job_env_overrides.json`, written by the Settings screen
3. the **process environment** — `rackstatus.toml`, the shell, the container
4. the platform's **low overlay** — geometry and per-tool defaults

`Reader` below says which rung a setting starts at. `ladder` means it is read through
`_eget` and therefore honours all four; `environment` means it is read straight from the
process environment and cannot be set per cluster or from the Settings screen.

## Undescribed settings

3 settings have no declaration, no prose in `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`
and no hint in `docs/settings-hints.toml`. Each name links to its row in the table
below, which still gives you its reader, its default and the module that reads it.

They are listed because an inventory that hid them would be the reason nobody knew. A
generator must not invent a description, so each of these is a real to-do — write one
into `docs/settings-hints.toml` and it moves out of this list on the next build.

<a href="#s-nvis-log-dir"><code>NVIS_LOG_DIR</code></a>, <a href="#s-rack-bringup-report-benchmarks"><code>RACK_BRINGUP_REPORT_BENCHMARKS</code></a>, <a href="#s-rack-bringup-report-job-status"><code>RACK_BRINGUP_REPORT_JOB_STATUS</code></a>

## Declared, read indirectly

4 settings are declared but never appear in a call this scan can see:
the connection profile reads its four by name from a list, and `NVIS_LOG_LEVEL` goes
through `logging_config`'s own registry. They are configuration like any other — the
scan simply cannot point at a call site.

`NVIS_LOG_LEVEL`, `RACK_SSH_KEY`, `RACK_SSH_PORT`, `RACK_SSH_USER`

## Read outside the resolution ladder

160 of them are read only via `os.environ`, so a cluster overlay and the
Settings screen cannot influence them — the setting is process-wide. New code should
prefer `_eget` (`core-designs.mdc` §5); these are the ones that predate the rule or
genuinely belong to the process rather than to a cluster.

They are not listed here — 160 names in a paragraph is not something
anyone reads.
The table below marks each one `environment` in its `Reader` column, which answers the
same question setting by setting, where you are already looking.

## Declared settings

These have a declaration, so `rackstatus.toml` can set them and the preflight can require
them. `UI` marks the ones the dashboard Settings screen may override.

| Setting | Section | Type | Required | UI | Example | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NEMO_SQSH_SRC` | validation | string | no |  | `/cluster/containers/nvidia+nemo+26.04.01-arm.sqsh` | Squashed NeMo container image used by the NeMo validation launchers. |
| `NVIS_FORCE_SETUP_WIZARD` | general | boolean | no |  | `false` | Re-open the first-run setup wizard even though a project is already configured. What `cli.py serve --setup-wizard` sets; normally left unset, since the wizard offers itself when no operator-created project exists. |
| `NVIS_LOG_LEVEL` | general | string | no |  | `INFO` | Log level. Settable here because the config file is read before logging is configured, which is the reason the loader's own records appear slightly late. |
| `RACK_BUG_REPORT_REMOTE_DIR` | connection | string | no |  | `/home/cmods/bringup-data/reports` | Base directory the bug-report and NVLMapper outputs are written to on each node (pdsh) and read from on the dashboard host (the Reports page). Point it at the project's own prefix -- a directory the service account can create and the dashboard host can see over the shared mount. Default /home/cmsupport/reports exists on only one appliance, so most deployments set this. NVLMapper's base (RACK_NVLMAPPER_REPORTS_BASE) defaults to it, so one value moves both. |
| `RACK_EXEC_MODE` | connection | string | no |  | `ssh` | How commands reach the cluster: 'ssh' or 'local'. Deprecated in favour of the topology-based transport config, and 'ssh' is the default; kept because deployed sites still set it. |
| `RACK_PLATFORM` | cluster | string | no |  | `bcm` | Cluster manager provider: 'bcm' (Base Command Manager) or 'maas'. |
| `RACK_PROJECT_TOKEN` | nvftp | string | no |  | `my-project` | NVFTP project folder name. Not a credential, despite matching the sensitive-name pattern on 'TOKEN'. |
| `RACK_REMOTE_BASE_PATH` | connection | string | no |  | `/home/cmsupport/nvis-rack-status` | Where the tooling is deployed on the head node. Script paths and the default log directory derive from it. Optional: unset falls back to the repo root, and a declared topology's scripts role root supersedes it. |
| `RACK_SLURM_SKIP_MODULE_LOAD` | cluster | boolean | no |  | `true` | Skip 'module load slurm' before scheduler commands, for sites where Slurm is already on PATH. |
| `RACK_SSH_HOST` | connection | string | no |  | `10.0.0.1` | Head node for the SSH control connection. Required unless the deployment is in demo mode or RACK_EXEC_MODE=local. |
| `RACK_SSH_KEY` | connection | string | no |  | `/run/secrets/ssh_key` | Path to the private key for the control connection. The path, not the key: the key itself must never appear in this file. |
| `RACK_SSH_PORT` | connection | integer | no |  | `22` | Port for the SSH control connection. |
| `RACK_SSH_USER` | connection | string | no |  | `root` | Account for the SSH control connection to the head node. |
| `RACK_STATUS_DEMO` | general | boolean | no |  | `false` | Synthetic data, no cluster contact. True on a developer laptop, and it also exempts the connection settings from the required-setting preflight. |
| `RACK_STATUS_LOG_DIR` | connection | string | no |  | `/home/cmsupport/aihpc_val-main/validation/nemo` | Deprecated. The directory Rack Status ingests node logs from. This is one global value for every cluster at once, so a multi-tenant deployment would read a project's logs from a cluster it may not operate; set the log directory per cluster instead (the cluster's connection.log_dir). Kept only as a fallback for deployments still migrating, and it warns when used. |
| `RACK_WEB_OIDC_ISSUER` | auth | string | no |  | `https://rackstatus.example.com` | This deployment's own base URL, used as the OIDC `iss` claim. Required when the OIDC provider is enabled. Cannot be derived from the request: OIDC Discovery 1.0 §4.3 requires it to be the URL discovery is served from, and a Host header is attacker-controlled. http is accepted only for localhost, which is how an operator reaches a tunnelled deployment. |
| `RACK_WEB_TLS_KEY` | tls | string | no |  | `/app/config/tls/server.key` | Private key for the TLS certificate. Required whenever RACK_WEB_TLS_CERT is set: a cert with no key downgrades one path silently and crashes the other. |

## Every setting

`What it controls` is the registry's own description where a setting has a declaration,
then a reviewed hint from `docs/settings-hints.toml`, then a pointer to the prose in
`docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`. A dash means nobody has written one yet.

`Reader` is `ladder` where the value goes through `_eget`, `environment` where it is read
straight from `os.environ`, and `indirect` for the five consumed by name from a list (the
connection profile) or through another registry (`logging_config`) rather than by a call
this scan can see. `Default` is shown only where the call site supplies a literal.

| <a id="s-rack-ssh-known-hosts"></a>`RACK_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS` | ladder |  | Path to a known_hosts file. Setting it turns on real host-key verification (StrictHostKeyChecking=yes plus IdentitiesOnly) for every SSH connection the app itself opens: the control connection to the head, the web terminal, the first leg of a declared hop chain or topology endpoint, bug-report collection, and bin/deploy-scripts.sh. That closes the machine-in-the-middle gap on a tunnelled or multi-hop path. Unset -- the default -- accepts any key, because an appliance's key changes when it is reimaged. Seed with `ssh-keyscan -H <head>`. Legs to compute nodes, and legs that run on a cluster host, are never verified; see backend/transport/hop.py. | `backend/transport/ssh.py` |

| <a id="s-rack-ssh-user"></a>`RACK_SSH_USER` | indirect |  | Account for the SSH control connection to the head node. |  |

| <a id="s-rack-web-oidc-issuer"></a>`RACK_WEB_OIDC_ISSUER` | environment |  | This deployment's own base URL, used as the OIDC `iss` claim. Required when the OIDC provider is enabled. Cannot be derived from the request: OIDC Discovery 1.0 §4.3 requires it to be the URL discovery is served from, and a Host header is attacker-controlled. http is accepted only for localhost, which is how an operator reaches a tunnelled deployment. | `backend/identity/oidc.py` |
